question: According to Global Debt Report 2025, what was the share of central bank holdings of domestic sovereign bonds in OECD countries in 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.19**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Global Debt Report 2025, the share of central bank holdings of domestic sovereign bonds in OECD countries in 2024 was **19% (0.19).**
 
• OECD countries represent economically advanced nations, including key players such as the US, UK, Japan, and European Union member states.
 
• The significant holding of domestic sovereign bonds by central banks highlights their role in stabilizing economies and managing fiscal policies.
 
• The increase in central bank holdings has been influenced by quantitative easing policies implemented during economic downturns.
 
• This share underscores the growing reliance on central banks to provide liquidity and maintain economic stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development):**

 
 
• An intergovernmental organization established in 1961 to promote economic progress and global trade.
 
• It consists of 38 member countries, mostly developed economies.
 
• OECD provides a platform for economic analysis and policy recommendations.
 
 
 
• **Domestic Sovereign Bonds:**
 
 
• Sovereign bonds are debt securities issued by governments to finance their expenditures.
 
• Domestic sovereign bonds are denominated in the issuing country’s local currency.
 
• Central banks often purchase these bonds as part of monetary policy measures.
 
 
 
• **Quantitative Easing (QE):**
 
 
• A monetary policy tool used by central banks to inject liquidity into the economy.
 
• Involves large-scale purchases of government bonds and other securities.
 
• Aimed at reducing interest rates and stimulating economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Economic Stability and Liquidity Management:**
 
 
• Central banks play a key role in maintaining economic stability by controlling inflation and managing liquidity.
 
• Purchasing sovereign bonds is one method to ensure adequate liquidity in financial markets.
